_doc: The repos agentctl's red machine watches (the owner, 2026-10-30, ci-failures recommendation 4: infra's Stage NixOS closures was red 29 h and core's Main Pipeline 21 h with no fixer). One entry per GitHub repo: `gate` its gate workflows ([name, file]: the newest decided run of each opens and clears its reds), `family` the red family every red of the repo belongs to (red-families.json says how it is held: one fixer per family), `push` `land` (its fixer lands with `agentctl land`) or `owner-only` (its fixer prepares the fix on a local branch and files the owner a one-liner with `agentctl red owner-push`; it never pushes or deploys: an infra push IS a deploy), `clone` the laptop's checkout fixers' worktrees branch from. `red_workflows` (optional, default false; the primary's built-in default true): the repo keeps .github/red-workflows.tsv on main, so a Fixes-Red landing while it is missing there is refused rather than read as "no replay" (lib/agentctl/red.py FIX REPLAY). The primary repo (movies) takes no `gate`: its gate is its own .github/gating-checks.tsv on main (lib/agentctl/ciwhy.py gate_flows); it keeps its outside workflows, local checks and landing gate. $AGENTCTL_RED_REPOS names another file. `generated` (optional): the repo's GENERATED files ([{paths, regen, timeout}]: lib/agentctl/waiting.py GENERATED FILES ARE NO OVERLAP), never an overlap that holds a queued change, and resolved on a rebase or a batch's assembly row by row, else by `regen` (the repo's own --update command, run in the tree).
